title: Playing 'If Ever I Cease to Love' from the Southland record
summary: A record of the song is played; Wiggs and Allen guess it was made 12-15 years earlier and praise its relaxed feel.

bands.name: Johnny Wiggs and His New Orleans Kings

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: In a house, in a square, in a quadrant, in a street, in a lane, in a road. Turn to the left on the right hand, you'll see there my true love's a bone. I go there according and going to my love like a turtle dove. And it's wearing on my bending knee, if ever I cease to love. May the sheep's head grow on apple trees, if ever I cease to love. If ever I cease to love, yes, if ever I cease to love. May the moon be turned to green, green cheese, if ever I cease to love. 된된 된 ! The End
The End That of course is Johnny Wiggs and his New Orleans Kings. The vocal was done by Dr. Edmund Sushon. Mr. Wiggs, how long ago was that recorded, sir?
I guess about 12 years or 15 years, wasn't it, Dick? Seems to me it was about 15 years ago. You were at that session, weren't you?

No, I heard the band many times down at the Woodman of the World Hall. Yeah. We used to play on Saturday nights there. Mm-hmm. With Raymond Burke and Emil Christian. Mm-hmm. It certainly was a wonderful band. I like the ending of that particularly myself. Thank you.
Nice relax? I like the relaxedness of the record.
